description: Reviewed cases for F24 Intended-use applicability and its physical-state boundary.

cases.source: EFSA FoodEx2 revision 2 p35-36; FoodEx2 maintenance 2016-2018 p18 Table 8
cases.question: A selected FoodEx2 term describes an uncooked physical state, and reporting must distinguish that the product is intended to be eaten cooked. Which facet family represents that intended-use distinction?
cases.reference_answer: Use F24 Intended-use for the intended-use distinction. F24 is single-cardinality and is applicable to all food types; it is not restricted to microbiology. The physical-state wording helps identify the documented catalogue pattern, but the reason to use F24 is that intended use must be represented.

cases.question: A product description states only that the food is liquid and gives no intended-use distinction. Does that physical-state wording by itself require F24 Intended-use?
cases.reference_answer: No. Physical-state wording alone does not require F24. Use F24 only when an intended-use distinction actually needs to be represented for the selected term or product; physical state belongs to its own coding decision.
